skill.name: Zone Index Encoding
skill.description: Encode zone information in an inverted index structure to support zone-aware document retrieval. Choose between dictionary-based encoding (zone labels as field extensions) or postings-based encoding (zone metadata in postings lists) based on query patterns and index constraints.
skill.skill_body:
When constructing an inverted index for multi-zone documents, decide whether to encode zone information as extensions in dictionary entries or embed it in postings lists. Dictionary encoding is compact for few zones; postings encoding is flexible for zone-weighted scoring. Ensure zone metadata is accessible during query evaluation.

## Objective

Store and retrieve zone metadata efficiently during query processing
## Applicable Signals

- Document collection has multiple fields or zones (e.g., author, title, abstract)
- Query logic requires zone filtering or zone-specific term weights

## Contraindications

- Single-field documents with no zone distinction
- Zone information not required for retrieval logic
- Extreme memory constraints where any metadata overhead is prohibitive

## Workflow Steps

- {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify all zones in the document collection', 'detail': 'List distinct fields or zones (e.g., author, title, abstract, language)'}
- {'step': 2, 'action': 'Evaluate encoding trade-offs', 'detail': 'Dictionary encoding: compact, suitable for few zones; postings encoding: flexible, suitable for zone-weighted scoring'}
- {'step': 3, 'action': 'Choose encoding strategy', 'detail': 'Select dictionary-based (zone as field extension) or postings-based (zone in postings list) based on query patterns and index size'}
- {'step': 4, 'action': 'Implement zone metadata storage', 'detail': 'Encode zone labels in chosen location; ensure consistent format across all postings or dictionary entries'}
- {'step': 5, 'action': 'Verify zone accessibility', 'detail': 'Confirm zone metadata is retrievable during query processing for zone filtering or weighted scoring'}

## Constraints

- Zone labels must be consistently defined across all documents
- Encoding choice must be decided before index construction begins
- Zone metadata must remain accessible during query evaluation

## Cautions

- Zone encoding decision is made at index construction time and affects all subsequent queries
- Changing encoding strategy requires index rebuild
- Zone metadata overhead increases index size; balance against query performance gains

## Output Contract

- Index structure with zone metadata embedded and accessible during query evaluation. Postings or dictionary entries include zone labels. Zone information is available for zone-restricted retrieval and zone-weighted scoring.
